title: Breaking the Bottleneck: User-Specific Optimization and Real-Time Inference Integration for Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Sequential recommendation models commonly apply the same inference model across users, neglecting individual user behavior patterns.

gap.claim: Parameter expansion can reach a performance limit when the data scale is fixed, leaving a bottleneck that user-specific sequence optimization may address.

contributions.claim: PCRec-simple performs one-time KL-divergence optimization on each user interaction sequence after training.
PCRec integrates real-time hidden-state inference into sequential recommendation and applies KL-divergence optimization during the forward process.

author_reported_evidence.claim: PCRec-simple is reported to provide additional insights and overcome the performance bottleneck after scaling laws.
Experiments on real-world datasets are reported to show that PCRec significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods.
The authors report that code is available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Sequential recommendation is presented as commercially valuable and widely studied.
Scaling laws and parameter expansion face limits with fixed data, while unified inference can neglect user-specific behavior.
PCRec-simple tests post-training, per-sequence KL-divergence optimization.
PCRec incorporates real-time hidden-state inference and forward-process KL-divergence optimization for end-to-end optimization.
Experiments on real-world datasets report significant improvement over current state-of-the-art methods.
